annotation.title_clean: Empowerment As Replacement for the Three Laws of Robotics
annotation.title_en: Empowerment As Replacement for the Three Laws of Robotics
annotation.summary_en: Hypothesis and theory paper proposing information-theoretic empowerment as an operational, non-language-based heuristic for robot behaviour that captures the intent of Asimov's Three Laws: self-preservation, protecting humans, and responding to human actions. Demonstrated through proof-of-principle simulations rather than legal or policy governance.
key_provisions_or_claims: Empowerment can serve as a generic, operational heuristic for robot behaviour in human interaction.
Maximising human empowerment operationalises 'do not harm' and 'do not allow harm' without natural language understanding.
Self-empowerment captures self-preservation; human-empowerment dependent on robot captures protection.
Offers an alternative to crude kill-switch safety approaches.
Not a complete account of ethical robot behaviour; safety and compliance are secondary to the main mission.
